title: EIA: 93 U.S. reactors at 54 plants as of 1 August 2023
summary: As of 1 August 2023 the EIA counts 93 operating reactors at 54 plants in 28 states, and a 2021 country table with the United States at 778.15 billion kWh.
body: The EIA nuclear page says nuclear power plants have generated about 20 percent of U.S. electricity since 1990. As of August 1, 2023, it counts 93 nuclear reactors operating at 54 plants in 28 states: 19 plants with one reactor, 31 with two, and 4 with three. Its 2021 table of the top five countries by nuclear capacity, sourced to EIA International Energy Statistics as of August 7, 2023, lists the United States at 95.49 million kilowatts, 778.15 billion kilowatthours, and 19 percent of national generation; France at 61.37 million kilowatts, 360.70 billion kilowatthours, and 68 percent; China at 53.26, 407.52, and 5 percent; Russia at 27.73, 222.44, and 20 percent; South Korea at 24.43, 150.52, and 26 percent. The page says that in 2021, 33 countries had commercial nuclear plants and that in 15 of them nuclear energy supplied at least 20 percent of annual electricity. The "about 20 percent since 1990" sentence and the 2023 table's 18.6 percent are different statements, a long-run description and one preliminary year. Last updated on the nuclear page: August 21, 2023, data as of August 7, 2023.
